objects.boundary: BrowserContext does not define native profile persistence, locking, policy, or budgets
CDP session is a client attachment, not the native engine authority
observed by the synthetic G2 court; HTML engines and external clients remain unqualified

one-to-one with a native frame while both live, adapter-scoped and not stable across adapters; qualified through Page.getFrameTree on the synthetic host (main frame plus one bounded child) and on the native route (one main frame) where puppeteer-core 24.15.0 observes it over a loopback edge and keeps the same id across a same-frame navigation; Page.frameNavigated and child-frame nesting are not projected; document generation has no CDP equivalent

realm identity and retirement are native; no Runtime.enable, executionContextCreated or executionContextDestroyed is projected in this increment, so a CDP client cannot observe realm replacement except through stale DOM handles after navigation
target activation is not presentation attachment
maintained by the native target and adapter
CDP IDs never bypass target revision validation

losses.loss: no CDP concept; Page.loaderId is the closest and is not mapped
target.navigate exists in 0.0.2 and maps onto Page.navigate; Page.frameNavigated and every other navigation event stay unprojected because this version projects no events at all

the synthetic host has exactly one bounded child frame and the native host builds bounded, same-origin, depth-one children; both project flat, each frame carries its own final url, and no nesting is offered
only the main world exists on the synthetic host; isolated worlds are unprojected
ignoreCache and scriptToEvaluateOnLoad have no native meaning and are refused typed rather than ignored

both stay -32601 unless the host remains the sole history authority: adapter-scoped ids would have to map onto host-minted entry identities, with an evicted, foreign or stale id failing typed. The adapter never keeps its own list, never renumbers and never answers from a cache. The native window is bounded and addressed by a signed delta, so CDP entry ids are not projected

an entry is the final canonical committed URL and, at most, a host-minted identity: no document, realm, body, form, scroll, script, cookie or storage state is retained, so a client that expects restored page state after going back gets a fresh document. Recorded, never emulated

losses.native: form value, checked state and selection
losses.loss: none of these is a typed form action: CDP either sets a node's text or replays raw key events. The adapter projects none of them and they stay -32601, because mapping a typed action onto raw key replay would claim an input path this host does not have

losses.cdp: Page.navigate after a client-side form serialisation
losses.loss: not projected: the adapter would have to serialise the form itself, which would make it a second authority over form state. The native submit serialises inside the realm and navigates through the same atomic path
not projected: only enter and space exist natively, and the CDP method implies a full keyboard, modifiers and key repeat that this host does not model

losses.native: form roles and their bounded facts
losses.loss: the checkbox, radio, select and form roles, their options and controls, and the disabled and read-only flags have no CDP equivalent and are visible only through the native door
